channel.title: Linux on DAWN's Blog
channel.description: Recent content in Linux on DAWN's Blog

item.title: Redis Core Practice (Part 2): Five Core Data Types, MySQL Hot Cache, and Transaction Features
item.description: Part 2 of the Redis Core Practice series: In-depth analysis of global key lifecycle management (keys/scan/expire/ttl), hands-on practice with Strings, Hash, List, Set, and SortedSet data structures, real-world implementations including high-concurrency counters, WeChat comment streams, friend topology, and TopN leaderboards, importing MySQL 3308 multi-instance hot rows into Redis Hash via Linux pipes, and in-depth comparison between MySQL ACID transactions and Redis weak transactions with WATCH optimistic locking.

item.title: Redis Core Practice (Part 1): Service Deployment, Security Hardening, and Persistence Mechanisms
item.description: Part 1 of the Redis Core Practice series: Systematically reviews Redis cache service positioning and comprehensive comparison with Memcached/Tair, provides step-by-step guidance on source compilation and installation, environment variables, and multi-instance planning under Linux, deeply analyzes the protected-mode mechanism and bind/requirepass security hardening, and details the underlying principles and trade-offs of RDB snapshots and AOF append logs.

item.title: Shell Scripting Hands-on (Part 3): Loops, Function Packaging, Expect Automation, and Array Statistics
item.description: A comprehensive guide to for and while loops in Shell, along with high-concurrency background network scanning. Master loop flow control (break, continue, exit), modular function design, automated interactive tasks via expect, and advanced indexed and associative arrays for data aggregation, frequency counting, and deduplicated random lottery algorithms.

item.title: Shell Scripting Hands-on (Part 2): Arithmetic Operations, Condition Tests, and Case Flow Control
item.description: An in-depth analysis of 6 arithmetic methods in Linux (expr, $(()), $[], let, bc, awk). Systematically covers test, [], and [[]] conditional tests and regex pattern matching, demonstrates if-elif branching for disk monitoring and OS version adaptation, and explores case statements to build interactive menus, Nginx service management, and Jumpserver architecture.

item.title: Shell Scripting Hands-on (Part 1): Script Specifications, Variable Classification, and String Slicing/Substitution
item.description: A systematic review of enterprise-grade Shell script development and execution standards. Deep dive into global environment variables, local variables, and special positional parameters ($0-$9, $#, $*, $@, $?). Master advanced native Bash string parameter expansion techniques including slicing, length evaluation, greedy pattern truncation, and substitution.

item.title: Linux awk Text Analysis Tool: From Syntax Principles to Nginx Access Log Statistics
item.description: A systematic analysis of awk, one of the three core Linux text processing tools. Covers its working mechanism and lifecycle (BEGIN/BODY/END), core internal variables and printf formatting, pattern matching, conditional/loop control, and 11 real-world enterprise Nginx log analysis scenarios utilizing associative arrays.

item.title: Linux sed Stream Editor Hands-on: Pattern Space and Hold Space
item.description: An in-depth analysis of the core architecture of sed (Stream Editor), systematically reviewing common options and editing actions, deeply dissecting the interaction mechanism between Pattern Space and Hold Space, and demonstrating multi-editing, inverted selection, and batch configuration cleanup based on enterprise practical cases.

item.title: Linux Hands-on Basics: Regular Expressions (BRE/ERE) and grep Text Filtering
item.description: A systematic review of Basic Regular Expressions (BRE) and Extended Regular Expressions (ERE) in Linux operations, deeply analyzing grep text filtering commands based on the dawn host across 14 core practical cases.
